title: Telemetry outcome event (v1)
description: One record in the local-first outcome store (design.md §13.1-§13.3, ADR-0004). This schema is where the privacy posture becomes STRUCTURAL rather than advisory. Four prohibitions are hard defaults that hold with zero configuration: (1) store no raw prompt text; (2) store no tool-result bodies; (3) store no secrets; (4) hash root session identifiers with a local salt, so cross-machine correlation is impossible by design rather than merely disabled. Enforcement is by construction in TWO layers, because a closed property set alone constrains only field NAMES and would leave every permitted field free to carry arbitrary text. Layer one: the property set below is a closed allowlist and `additionalProperties` is false at every object level. Layer two: every property that accepts a string also constrains its VALUE — `root_session_hash` must match `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`, a fixed-width hex digest that structurally cannot hold a raw Hermes session id or prompt text; `event_id` is at most 64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`; `lane_id` and `candidate` are at most 128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`; `decision_id` is `dec_` plus at most 64 alphanumerics, anchored at both ends; `error_class` is a classification capped at 64 characters; `feedback` is a two-valued enum; `occurred_at` is an anchored RFC 3339 timestamp. Every remaining property is a bounded number or a boolean. The result is that no property in this schema — under any name, spelling, or value — has room to carry request content, response content, tool arguments, tool-result bodies, error bodies, or credential values, and widening either layer requires a schema version bump and the review that implies. External export remains opt-in and may emit only a subset of these fields (design.md §13.5).

event_id.description: Opaque unique identifier for this event. Bounded length and an identifier-only character class, so this field cannot be repurposed as a free-text carrier.

event_type.description: Event family (design.md §13.1-§13.3). Determines which of the optional measurement fields are meaningful; the schema does not require any of them, because collection is best-effort and a provider may not report every measurement.

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp at which the event occurred. The `pattern` is what actually enforces the shape: `format` is annotation-only under JSON Schema 2020-12 and is inert unless a validator is explicitly configured with a format checker, so it is kept as documentation but never relied on.

root_session_hash.description: Root session identifier hashed with a LOCAL salt (ADR-0004, design.md §13.1). Never the raw Hermes session id. The pattern is what makes that structural rather than advisory: only a 64-character lowercase hex digest validates, so a raw session id, a prompt, or a credential cannot be written here even by a future code path that tries. Because the salt is local, the same conversation on two machines hashes differently and fleet-level correlation is unavailable by construction.

lane_id.description: Opaque lane identifier within the root session (design.md §6.2). An opaque handle, not a derived or reversible value. Bounded length and an identifier-only character class keep it a handle rather than a text field.

decision_id.description: The RouteDecision this outcome is attributed to, joining the event to its explainability record. Anchored at BOTH ends: a prefix-only `^dec_` would have accepted `dec_` followed by an arbitrary payload.

candidate.description: The `id` of the model card whose candidate produced this outcome. Bounded to the character class model-card ids are drawn from.

ttft_ms.description: Time to first token in milliseconds (design.md §13.2).

input_tokens.description: Actual uncached input token count as normalized by Hermes (design.md §13.2). A count only — the tokens themselves are never stored.

output_tokens.description: Actual output token count (design.md §13.2). A count only.

cached_tokens.description: Actual cache-read token count (design.md §13.2). A count only.

reasoning_tokens.description: Actual reasoning token count (design.md §13.2). A count only; hidden model reasoning is never captured or reconstructed (design.md §12).

actual_cost_usd.description: Actual turn cost in USD (design.md §13.2). Null means the cost is unknown — for example an unpriced local candidate — and unknown is never reconciled as zero (design.md §7.5).

tool_call_count.description: Number of tool calls in the turn (design.md §13.2). A count only; tool names, arguments, and results are not stored.

invalid_tool_call_count.description: Number of malformed or rejected tool calls (design.md §13.2). A count only.

empty_response.description: Whether the candidate returned an empty response (design.md §13.2). A flag only, never the response body.

context_compressed.description: Whether context compression ran for this request (design.md §13.2).

user_interrupted.description: Whether the user interrupted the turn (design.md §13.2).

feedback.description: Explicit positive or negative user feedback (design.md §13.3). A two-valued enum, deliberately not free text, so a user comment can never become a content-retention channel.

error_class.description: Short machine-readable failure classification such as `rate_limit`, `auth_failure`, `context_overflow`, `timeout`, or `upstream_5xx`. This is a CLASSIFICATION assigned by the router, never a captured error body, provider message, stack trace, or response payload. `maxLength` is a deliberate second barrier against a future implementation pasting a message body into this field.
